git add src/codegen/lower_inst/method_resolution.rs src/types/checker/builtin_spl_classes/storage.rs tests/codegen/spl.rs tests/codegen/spl/array_object_missing_key.rs && git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(spl): reading an absent ArrayObject key answered NULL and said nothing

php raises `Undefined array key <k>` for it, exactly as it does for a plain array, and
answers NULL. elephc answered NULL in SILENCE — the value was right, the diagnostic
missing. MEASURED on `php -n` 8.5.6 across both classes and both spellings,
`offsetGet($k)` and `$o[$k]` on `ArrayObject` and `ArrayIterator`: six warnings, none of
which elephc raised. The plain-array spelling one line away warned correctly, which is what
made the gap easy to miss and easy to confirm.

The key's RENDERING is part of the message — an int bare, a string quoted — so the miss
path reads a key out of an EMPTY array rather than composing a second message: php's own
way of raising it, through the runtime path a plain array already uses. An assoc literal
and not `[]`, because an `array<never>` index folds to null at compile time, warning and
all.

The LINE needed the other half. A synthesized body publishes no span of its own, so it
inherits whatever the call site published — and a call into one of these classes may not
publish, because the effect refinement unions the summaries of every class the receiver
could hold and drops the whole answer when one of them has none, leaving effects that do
not mention warnings. `(new ArrayIterator([1]))->offsetGet(7)` raised its warning with NO
` in FILE on line N` at all, while the `ArrayObject` spelling of the same call, whose
summary did resolve, named its line correctly. The call site now publishes the line in both
the forms an internal diagnostic can want — the number a throwable stores, and the rendered
suffix a warning appends.
